Portugal · 2003–2026

Hand back the 7

Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football after 23 years, 234 caps and a record 146 goals for Portugal.

For 23 years, one number belonged to one man in Portugal’s team.

Inside that 7 are 146 international goals, more than any man in the history of the sport.

On November 5, 2026, aged 41, he said: “The day has come for me to hand back the number 7 shirt of our national team.”

Hand back the 7.

Where it began

The boy in No. 17

Before the 7, there was the 17. Ronaldo burst onto the international stage as a teenager at Euro 2004, on home soil, as Portugal reached the final.

The son

The boy from Madeira

Long before the records, he was the youngest of four children in a working-class family on a small Atlantic island.

“Ronaldo”Named after US president Ronald Reagan, a favourite of his father
Age 12Left home alone for Sporting CP’s academy in Lisbon, more than 950km away
2005Lost his father, José, when he was 20, two years into his Portugal career
2017Madeira’s airport was renamed Cristiano Ronaldo International Airport
Six World Cups

Around the world

0World Cup goals

Ronaldo played at six World Cups, from Germany in 2006 to North America in 2026.

He scored at every one of them, the first man ever to do so.

His three goals in 2026 took him to 11, past Eusébio’s Portugal record. But Portugal went out in the round of 16, beaten 1–0 by Spain.

The final chapter

An unceremonious end

Summer 2026
A sixth World Cup

Three goals, a record, then a 1–0 defeat to Spain in the round of 16. Afterwards he admitted he had considered retiring, but chose to carry on.

September 2026
The last game

A 1–0 win against Wales in Lisbon: cap number 234.

October 2026
The row

Left as an unused substitute against Norway in the Nations League, he accused new coach Jorge Jesus of breaking promises over playing time and walked out of the camp. The federation suspended him for 30 days.

November 5, 2026
Goodbye

Days after the suspension ended, he announced his retirement in a video on Instagram.

Portugal coach Jorge Jesus

What comes next

The end of an era

The rival
Messi, too

Ronaldo’s announcement came shortly after Lionel Messi retired from international football with Argentina. Football’s defining rivalry is over on the international stage.

The last chase
985 / 1,000

He plays on for Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia, 15 goals short of 1,000 career goals for club and country.

146 goals. 23 years.

One shirt nobody else can fill.
